primary_sources: Docker Production Security & Multi-Stage Building Guidelines

rules.rule_name: Multi-Stage Docker Builds and Minimal Images
rules.explanation: Including compilers, SDKs, and build toolchains in final container production images drastically increases image size and attack surface.
rules.do: Utilize multi-stage Docker builds and deploy final binaries/artifacts onto minimal base images (e.g., Alpine, Distroless, Scratch).
rules.dont: Do not ship heavy full OS distribution base images (e.g., Ubuntu/Debian default tags) containing build utilities to production registries.

rules.explanation: Running containers as the default root user allows potential container breakout exploits to compromise the underlying host OS kernel.
rules.do: Define explicit unprivileged system user groups (e.g., USER node/appuser) within Dockerfiles before execution commands.
rules.dont: Do not execute container entrypoint processes as the default root user inside production container environments.

rules.rule_name: Resource Limits and Quota Management in Kubernetes
rules.explanation: Deploying Pods without explicit memory and CPU boundaries enables noisy neighbor syndrome and causes Node Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes.
rules.do: Configure explicit resource requests and limits (CPU and Memory) for every container manifest in Kubernetes deployment specifications.
rules.dont: Do not launch unconstrained workloads into Kubernetes clusters without defining resource requests and limits.

rules.explanation: Without health probes, orchestrators route client traffic to unresponsive or initializing containers, leading to failed requests.
rules.do: Implement precise liveness, readiness, and startup probes pointing to dedicated application health-check endpoints.
rules.dont: Do not rely strictly on process existence without verifying network-level application readiness and dependency health.
